description.narrative: In 1981, the Catholic Bishops Conference of Sierra Leone, established “Caritas Sierra Leone’ non-governmental faith-based organization, as the relief and development wing of the Catholic Church in Sierra Leone, operating countrywide, through a National office, and four diocesan offices. Since the start of the war in 1991, the structures of Caritas Sierra Leone collapsed, and from then on, the national office closed down, whilst the diocesan offices remained operational. Due to mounting humanitarian emergencies created by the war, each diocesan office responded separately, outside a national framework. Hence, whilst individual parts of the organization survived, the organization in its entirety collapsed, including the breakdown of the national board, the national management team, the national office, and the various coordinating structures. At a recent meeting of the technical taskforce charged with responsibility to translate the reports of the Road Mapping Workshop into a fundable proposal, the problems highlighted above were subjected to further reflections, by doing a problem tree analysis as well as a stakeholder analysis.
